reviewScope: Editorial review against the English descriptions in the pinned UNESCO 2025 CSV, not an independent archaeological redating. Intervals index the named phase only. Inclusive BCE centuries and millennia run from -N*unit to -(N-1)*unit-1; CE intervals start at (N-1)*unit+1. No year zero. Approximate dates retain their qualification. The selected date phrase is preserved for each interpretation.
attribution: Adapted from UNESCO World Heritage Centre, World Heritage Site List (2025), English property descriptions. Human Atlas adds phase labels, date indexing and explanatory notes.
disclaimer: The present work is not an official UNESCO publication and shall not be considered as such

1687.label: Neolithic permanent settlement attested
1687.note: UNESCO describes an already substantial settlement with a wall, ditch and tower by this period. This dates the attested Neolithic phase; it is neither the first human presence nor the lifetime of Jericho. The description also discusses later Bronze Age phases without numeric dates.

1572.label: Pre-Pottery Neolithic monuments
1572.note: Dates the monumental structures attributed to hunter-gatherers. Their ritual or funerary use is an interpretation, not a demonstrated single function.

1405.label: Eastern mound · Neolithic occupation
1405.note: The eastern mound contains eighteen occupation levels. The marker uses the UNESCO property coordinate and does not locate individual houses. This expands the existing Çatalhöyük historical moment with a separate site record.

1405.label: Western mound · Chalcolithic phase
1405.note: The later phase concerns the western mound. Keeping the two intervals separate preserves the change in location and archaeological period.

848.label: Neolithic settlement occupation
848.quote: occupied from the 7th to the 4th millennium B.C.
848.note: Broad occupation interval given in the description. The millennium endpoints are indexing bounds, not precise founding or abandonment years and not proof of uninterrupted habitation.

1592.label: Late Neolithic urban remains
1592.note: Dates the Liangzhu remains discussed in the description, including earthworks, water management and differentiated burials. One marker represents a property with four component areas.

1456.label: Bronze Age city · four occupation periods
1456.quote: Founded around 3200 BC, it was populated during four main periods up to 1800 BC
1456.note: This envelope contains four occupation periods, not a claim that every part of the city was inhabited continuously. The description links eventual abandonment to changing watercourses and climate.

941.label: Mycenaean cities in their regional context
941.quote: from the 15th to the 12th century B.C.
941.note: The stated interval concerns Mycenaean civilization's regional prominence. It does not date every surviving building or establish the truth of Homeric narratives. One coordinate represents Mycenae and Tiryns.

393.label: Delphi as a pan-Hellenic religious centre
393.note: UNESCO describes the sanctuary's religious importance during this century. The interval is a documented phase of significance, not the sanctuary's complete lifespan.

404.label: Classical monumental building programme
404.dateLabel: Second half of the 5th century BCE
404.quote: In the second half of the fifth century bc
404.note: Dates the period of the Athenian building programme described by UNESCO. The half-century bounds are a display convention, not exact construction dates for every monument.

517.label: Centre for the worship of Zeus
517.quote: In the 10th century B.C., Olympia became a centre for the worship of Zeus
517.note: The description also mentions earlier habitation without a numeric date. This interval concerns the religious development only.

517.label: Beginning of the Olympic Games in UNESCO's account
517.note: The date given for the beginning of the recurring games in this account. A single date marks that claim; it does not imply the games lasted for only one year.

377.label: Hittite capital · regional influence
377.note: A broad interval for the influence of Hattusha in Anatolia and northern Syria. It is not a precise reign, city foundation date, or set of empire boundaries.

1731.label: Lydian capital and tumuli
1731.note: Dates the Lydian cultural context of the capital and cemetery. Sardis continued under later rulers; the interval does not mark the end of the settlement.

1293.label: Nabataean monumental tombs
1293.quote: from the 1st century BC to the 1st century AD
1293.note: This range dates decorated tomb facades. The description separately mentions earlier inscriptions and drawings, so it must not become a date for the first occupation of Hegra.

977.label: Megalithic dolmen tombs
977.note: One property coordinate represents three concentrations of tombs. The interval dates the dolmens in the description, not a single cemetery's uninterrupted use.

1624.label: Archaeoastronomical ceremonial complex
1624.note: The complex used the Sun and its built horizon as a calendar. A solar cult is described as probable, and is not treated as certain.

15.label: Dated monumental remains at Aksum
15.quote: between the 1st and the 13th century A.D.
15.note: This broad envelope dates the surviving ruins described by UNESCO. It is not the lifespan of the Kingdom of Aksum or evidence for uninterrupted political dominance.

23.label: Palmyrene art and architecture
23.note: The description discusses the combination of Graeco-Roman, local and Persian traditions. CE is supplied by this historical context. This is a cultural phase, not a founding date.

198.label: Mississippian settlement
198.note: The primary occupation period in UNESCO's account. Local population estimates in the description are not injected into the HYDE grid.

198.label: Peak settlement phase
198.note: A narrower phase within the occupation interval. Overlapping phases still produce only one site marker and do not double-count population.

364.label: Shona city and trading centre
364.note: Dates the Shona civilization represented by the remains. The Queen of Sheba association elsewhere in the description is explicitly a legend and is not used as historical evidence.

449.label: Later modern-human remains
449.quote: Homo sapiens sapiens dating as far back as 18,000–11,000 B.C.
449.note: This is the description's date for later modern-human remains. It does not date the much older Peking Man remains and does not establish a migration corridor. Dating follows this source account rather than a new synthesis.

1645.label: Harappan urban occupation
1645.note: Dates occupation of the city in UNESCO's description, with fortifications, cemeteries and water management. The representative coordinate does not define its urban extent.

567.label: Tiwanaku at its apogee
567.quote: reached its apogee between 500 and 900 AD
567.note: This is a peak phase of the city and its political influence, not its foundation or abandonment interval.

1660.label: Construction of the Viking ring fortresses
1660.note: A building interval for five fortresses associated with the Jelling Dynasty. One UNESCO coordinate represents the serial property, not all five locations.

414.label: Teotihuacan monumental construction
414.quote: Built between the 1st and 7th centuries A.D.
414.note: Dates the urban construction described by UNESCO, not every phase of human activity in the area. The marker does not imply a measured population.

791.label: Uxmal building phase
791.quote: buildings, which date from between 700 and 1000
791.note: The interval concerns buildings in the description. Its approximate foundation and suggested population are separate claims, and no population is added to the grid.

524.label: Early Buddhist monuments
524.quote: most of which date back to the 2nd and 1st centuries B.C.
524.note: Most monuments discussed in the description belong to this phase. Sanchi remained an important Buddhist centre much later, so the end of the phase is not abandonment.

139.label: Buddhist centre of learning
139.quote: from the 5th century B.C. to the 2nd century A.D.
139.note: Dates Taxila's role as a centre of learning in this account. The property includes settlements from other periods; the single marker cannot locate all of them.

1528.label: Prehistoric settlements and burial structures
1528.quote: from the Bronze Age (1600 BCE) to the Late Iron Age (123 BCE)
1528.note: A broad envelope for the structures represented across Menorca, not uninterrupted use of every building. Astronomical and cosmological interpretations remain qualified.

4.label: Norse settlement remains
4.note: The source specifies a century, not a century-long occupation. This interval expresses date precision for the settlement remains, not the duration of continuous habitation.

208.label: Bamiyan artistic and religious developments
208.note: This broad interval concerns the artistic and religious developments summarized by UNESCO. The separately mentioned destruction in 2001 is not mistaken for the origin of the monuments.
